sentences.text: The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2038/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 18.11.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Nadiad in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.333 of 2018, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.11,58,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimants, holding all the opponents liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text: There is no dispute raised with regard to the facts of the case nor about the negligence aspect as considered by the Tribunal and hence, that aspect requires no mention.
2. Mr. Nishit Bhalodi, learned advocate appearing for the appellants submits that the deceased was aged about 38 years at the time of his death and he was maintaining his wife and two minor child.
Mr. Bhalodi, learned advocate further submitted that at the time accident, the deceased was doing job, but unfortunately could not place any cogent evidence, to substantiate the income.
The learned tribunal ought to have considered the minimum wages schedule keeping in mind the date of accident as 11.07.2017 and thus, has urged to consider the income accordingly.

Mr. Bhalodi, learned advocate further submits that the learned tribunal has placed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2038/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined reliance on the judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680, has considered 40% rise, which is consistent.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And accordingly, submitted that the rest of the calculation is in accordance to the judgment of Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma (supra)
except the fact that the learned tribunal has cut down the monthly income.
3. Countering the argument, Mr. Rahin Raval, learned advocate appearing for the Insurance Company has submitted that the assessment of income is in accordance to the facts and evidence.

He submits that there is no evidence on record that the deceased was working in the 'Khaman-shop'
and thus, could be considered only as a 'unskilled labour'.

Hence, it is stated by Mr. Raval, learned advocate for the Insurance Company that the learned tribunal has rather assessed the income on the higher-side, which to be decided on the line of minimum wages schedule approved by the State of Gujarat.
4. The learned tribunal has considered the income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- per month.

The minimum wages NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2038/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined schedule at the date of death of the deceased i.e. 11.07.2017 reflects the wages granted to the unskilled labourer as Rs.7,946/-.
Hence, this Court has considered just and reasonable the minimum wages for the deceased keeping in mind the minimum wages schedule as Rs.7,946/- per month.

2 5.

entities.text: Kusumben Jayantibhai Vaghela vs Imraanbhai Nazirbhai Vohra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The tribunal has followed the judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra) and given 40% rise in the future/
prospective income, while there is no error towards amount granted under the head of loss of consortium; funeral expenses and loss of estate.
6. Thus, considering the minimum wages as Rs.7,946/-, the dependency loss would come to Rs.13,34,880/-.
Rs.7,946/- Plus 40% prospective rise = Rs.11,124/-.

Considering the dependency,
1/3rd amount is deducted against the personal expenses of the deceased, thus, the monthly income would come to [Rs.11,124/- minus Rs.3,708/- (2/3rd amount)] = Rs.7,416/-.
7.

Considering the future monthly income as Rs.7,416/-, which is multiplied for 12 months and by applying 15 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2038/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined multiplier, the dependency loss would come to Rs.13,34,880/-.

Therefore, amount of Rs.13,34,880/-
is awarded towards loss of dependency.

8. Therefore, the appellants - claimants are entitled to get the the following final amount as compensation:-
 Particulars

Amount (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 13,34,880/-
 Consortium 1,20,000/-
 Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
 Total 14,84,880/-
9.
The learned tribunal has granted in-toto Rs.11,58,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum, which the Insurance Company required to be deposited.
The enhanced amount would come to Rs.3,26,880/-, which the Insurance Company shall deposit within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order.
It is directed that the enhanced amount would be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2038/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined 10.
In the facts and circumstances, the present appeal is partly allowed, with no order as to costs.

The judgment and award dated 18.11.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.),
Nadiad in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.333 of 2018 shall stand modified as aforesaid.

with accrued interest thereon if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
